A.source_reading: Either happy or sad is ambiguous between inclusive disjunction and exclusive categories. At least one happy event alone does not refute all sad events under inclusive disjunction: one happy-and-sad event makes all events sad, whereas one happy-only event refutes it. Hence Uncertain under inclusive reading. Under exclusive disjunction, the happy witness is not sad, so False.
A.answer_1: Source-supported under inclusive reading, not uniquely determined across ordinary readings.
A.answer_2: Source-supported under exclusive reading, not uniquely determined across ordinary readings.
A.premise_consistency: Both readings have consistent models; no need to invoke inconsistency/explosion.
A.utility: INCONCLUSIVE regardless of native label; preserve both interpretations and original annotation agreement, no answer correction or semantic gain credit.

B.source_reading: The supplied duster exists as a household appliance and does not suck. It is an explicit counterexample to every household appliance sucking. Other categories and space supply no needed inference.
B.answers: Both labels supported by the explicit counterexample.
B.assumptions: Ordinary existential reading of 'A duster is a household appliance that does not suck'; no outside facts about appliances or vampires.

C.source_reading: If John had any wedding, the first premise implies a child; the fifth premise then implies no wedding. Thus John has no wedding in any consistent classical interpretation, so he has no well-attended wedding. Some July weddings can belong to other people and do not force a John wedding. The last conditional does not assert its antecedent.
C.assumptions: Consistent classical inference, ordinary well-attended-wedding implies having a wedding; no invented John identity with owners of existential weddings.
C.premise_consistency: Assign John no child/wedding/Paris and give some other person a well-attended July wedding, child and Paris honeymoon. All premises can hold.

D.source_reading: KO is mature, hence suitable. Volatility would imply not suitable, so in any consistent classical reading KO is not volatile. A growth stock would be volatile, so KO is not a growth stock. The conclusion's growth-or-volatile antecedent is false, making its material conditional True even though KO is a company stock.
D.answers: Both labels source-supported for the task's classical conditional inference.
D.assumptions: Material implication and classical consistency; no claim that ordinary investment or conversational advice is vacuously informative, and no actual-world statement about KO.
D.premise_consistency: A separate growth stock can be volatile and unsuitable; KO mature, suitable and nonvolatile.
